Hi — putting together the packet now and summarizing key points below (so we can iterate quickly):

1) WHAT WE LOG (high-level)
- Console/admin actions: user sign-in, SSO events, role changes, invitations, MFA changes, service account/key creation and deletion, password resets.
- API events: token creation/rotation, model invocation metadata (request id, model id, model version, sequence length), caller identity (service account or user id), request timestamp, response size, latency metrics.
- Data actions: dataset uploads, dataset deletions, model payload uploads (file names only, payloads not stored in audit log), config changes (deployment, quantization profiles).
- Infrastructure: IP addresses, region, instance id, container/node id, kube pod id (redacted in customer exports by default).
- Error and security events: failed logins, rate limit violations, suspicious activity flags.

2) RETENTION POLICY (default)
- Raw, event-level audit logs: 395 days (13 months) retained in our hot store for customer support and SOC 2 evidence.
- Cold archive: 7 years aggregated summaries (daily/hourly rollups) for long-term compliance and trend analysis.
- Access logs for hosted endpoints (token-level): 90 days for detailed traces, with aggregated billing/usage metrics retained 24 months.
- Note: retention policies are configurable for Dedicated/Private customers via contract (we can offer custom retention in Dedicated and Private deployments; on-prem retention is customer-controlled).

3) EXPORT OPTIONS
- Console: Security > Audit Logs -> filter by date/actions -> Export (CSV/JSONL). Exports are redacted by default to remove PII unless a redaction waiver is signed.
- Scheduled exports: daily/weekly to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets (signed write role or presigned URL).
- API: /v1/admin/audit-exports (JSONL streaming or batch job). Auth via admin API key with audit scope.
- SIEM connectors: native Splunk HEC, Sumo Logic, Datadog Logs; we also support forwarding via Syslog over TLS.
- On-request auditor package: we prepare a zipped evidence bundle (JSONL sample, schema CSV, checksums, attestation letter) and deliver via secure Drive link or presigned S3 URL.

4) SAMPLE SCHEMA (summary)
- Fields: event_id, timestamp, actor_id, actor_type (user/service), action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, ip_address (redacted mask option), user_agent, request_payload_meta, response_status, latency_ms, region
- Full CSV schema attached as audit_log_schema_v2.csv.

5) REDACTION AND PII
- By default we mask the last octet of IPv4 addresses, truncate user_agent strings longer than 256 chars, and remove file payloads (we only record filenames/hashes). For auditor collections we can provide a redaction waiver process — legal signs off and we produce a restricted export.

6) AUDITOR ACCESS + TIMELINE
- Standard flow: request via account rep (Priyom) -> Security creates evidence bundle -> Bundle delivered via secure link (48–72 hour turnaround for standard requests).
- For SOC 2 in-process audits we can arrange live S3 exports for the auditor (requires customer approval + NDA).

I'll attach a redacted sample and the schema. Dev, please add the API call examples and any rate limits. Marissa — confirm if there are billing or contract notes for extended retention.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Adding technical details — paste below for inclusion in the packet: 

EXPORT ENDPOINTS / EXAMPLES
1) Console one-off export
- UI path: Console > Security > Audit Logs > [filter] > Export -> choose JSONL or CSV -> encrypted ZIP download.

2) Admin API (programmatic)
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/admin/audit-exports
- Body: {"start_time":"2026-02-01T00:00:00Z","end_time":"2026-02-28T23:59:59Z","format":"jsonl","destination":{"type":"s3","bucket":"acme-audit-uploads","prefix":"2026/02/"}}
- Response: job_id + presigned write URL for server-side push.
- Notes: max 5TB per job, chunked streaming supported. Jobs run in background; status endpoint available.

3) SIEM forwarding
- Splunk HEC token + index; we support ECS-compatible fields. Events are batched; typical throughput 2k EPS per cluster node.

RATE LIMITS & PERFORMANCE
- One-off export jobs: concurrency limited to 3 active jobs per account to protect cluster performance.
- Streaming API: 1,000 events/sec per org for hosted customers by default; Dedicated customers can request higher.

INFRA & STORAGE
- Hot store: Elasticsearch+S3 tiered architecture for 13-month hot retention (searchable).
- Cold: daily rollups stored in Glacier-equivalent (customer-archived), accessible via retrieval job (24–48 hours).

SECURITY & ATTORNEY REQUESTS
- Audit bundles are signed and checksummed; we log the delivery event and who accessed the bundle.

I'll attach a redacted sample export (acme_audit_sample.jsonl) and the export_instructions.pdf with API examples.

- Dev
Principal Engineer, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
